findings.evidence: `rg -n "#\[simp\].*revProcess|revProcess_apply|attribute \[simp\].*revProcess" code mathlib -S` finds only `TimeReversal.lean:41:lemma revProcess_apply ...`, with no simp attribute.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` to `revProcess_apply` so `simp` reduces `revProcess X N n ω` to `X (N - n) ω`; this is a one-way definitional equation and should not loop.
findings.issue: `revProcess_apply` is the normal-form characterization of the public `revProcess`, but it is not marked `@[simp]`, leaving downstream goals involving `(revProcess X N) n ω` stuck unless users explicitly rewrite by this lemma or unfold the definition.

summary: The public surface is minimal, but the characteristic API for the new public definition is not wired into simplification, so users must unfold or name the lemma manually to use `revProcess`.
